## Overview

This guide covers the full configuration of the Auggie Smith Photography
website on an Ubuntu server running nginx, including the Shiny CMS application
for photo uploads.

**Architecture**

| Component | Location | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Static site | `/srv/auggie-smith-photography/_site` | Quarto-rendered portfolio |
| CMS app | `/srv/auggie-smith-photography/cms` | Shiny photo upload interface |
| Images | `/srv/auggie-smith-photography/cms/images` | Uploaded photographs |
| Photo metadata | `/srv/auggie-smith-photography/cms/data/photos.json` | CMS data store |

---

## Prerequisites

- Ubuntu server with nginx installed
- Domain name pointed at the server
- SSH access with sudo privileges

---

## Step 1 — Install Git

```bash
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y
sudo apt install -y git
git --version
```

---

## Step 2 — Install R

```bash
sudo apt install -y software-properties-common dirmngr

wget -qO- https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/ubuntu/marutter_pubkey.asc \
  | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/r-project.gpg

echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/r-project.gpg] \
  https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/ubuntu $(lsb_release -cs)-cran40/" \
  | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/r-project.list

sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y r-base r-base-dev
```

---

## Step 3 — Install System Libraries

```bash
sudo apt install -y build-essential libcurl4-openssl-dev libssl-dev \
  libxml2-dev libfontconfig1-dev libharfbuzz-dev libfribidi-dev \
  libfreetype6-dev libpng-dev libtiff5-dev libjpeg-dev libuv1-dev
```

---

## Step 4 — Install Quarto

Check the latest release at <https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases>.
Confirm server architecture with `uname -m` — use `amd64` for x86_64 servers
and `arm64` for ARM servers.

```bash
wget -P /tmp \
  https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/download/v1.9.37/quarto-1.9.37-linux-amd64.deb

sudo gdebi /tmp/quarto-1.9.37-linux-amd64.deb
quarto --version
```

---

## Step 5 — Install Shiny Server

Check the latest Ubuntu/Debian installer at <https://posit.co/download/shiny-server/>.

```bash
wget -P /tmp \
  https://download3.rstudio.org/ubuntu-18.04/x86_64/shiny-server-1.5.22.1017-amd64.deb

sudo gdebi /tmp/shiny-server-1.5.22.1017-amd64.deb
sudo systemctl status shiny-server
```

---

## Step 6 — Install Required R Packages

```bash
sudo R -e "install.packages(
  c('shiny', 'bslib', 'jsonlite', 'DT', 'htmltools', 'tools'),
  repos = 'https://cloud.r-project.org'
)"
```

---

## Step 7 — Clone the Repository

```bash
sudo git clone https://github.com/justenvirons/auggie-smith-photography.git \
  /srv/auggie-smith-photography
```

---

## Step 8 — Set Permissions

The `shiny` user runs the Shiny Server process and must own the project
directory so it can write uploaded images and re-render the site.

```bash
sudo chown -R shiny:shiny /srv/auggie-smith-photography
```

---

## Step 9 — Initial Quarto Render

```bash
cd /srv/auggie-smith-photography
sudo -u shiny quarto render
```

Confirm `_site/` was created:

```bash
ls /srv/auggie-smith-photography/_site
```

---

## Step 10 — Configure Shiny Server

```bash
sudo nano /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf
```

Replace the contents with:

```nginx
run_as shiny;

server {
  listen 3838;

  location /cms {
    app_dir /srv/auggie-smith-photography/cms;
    log_dir /var/log/shiny-server;
  }
}
```

```bash
sudo systemctl restart shiny-server
sudo systemctl status shiny-server
```

---

## Step 11 — Obtain SSL Certificate

```bash
sudo apt install -y certbot python3-certbot-nginx

sudo certbot --nginx \
  -d auggie-smith-photography.com \
  -d www.auggie-smith-photography.com
```

Certbot automatically adds HTTP → HTTPS redirect blocks to `nginx.conf`.
Do not edit those blocks manually — Certbot manages them on renewal.

---

## Step 12 — Configure nginx

```bash
sudo nano /etc/nginx/sites-available/auggie-smith
```

```nginx
server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    server_name auggie-smith-photography.com www.auggie-smith-photography.com;

    ssl_certificate     /etc/letsencrypt/live/auggie-smith-photography.com/fullchain.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/auggie-smith-photography.com/privkey.pem;
    include             /etc/letsencrypt/options-ssl-nginx.conf;
    ssl_dhparam         /etc/letsencrypt/ssl-dhparams.pem;

    root  /srv/auggie-smith-photography/_site;
    index index.html;

    # Serve uploaded images as static files
    location /cms/images/ {
        try_files $uri =404;
    }

    # Proxy CMS app to Shiny Server
    location /cms {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3838/cms;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_read_timeout 20d;
        proxy_buffering off;
    }

    # Serve static site
    location / {
        try_files $uri $uri/ =404;
    }
}
```

Enable the site, disable the default, then test and reload:

```bash
sudo ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/auggie-smith \
           /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/auggie-smith

sudo rm /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default

sudo nginx -t
sudo systemctl reload nginx
```

---

## Step 13 — Verify the Setup

Open a browser and confirm:

| URL | Expected result |
|---|---|
| `https://auggie-smith-photography.com` | Static portfolio site |
| `https://auggie-smith-photography.com/cms` | CMS login screen |

---

## Ongoing Workflow

1. Log in at `https://auggie-smith-photography.com/cms`
2. Upload a photo with title, category, and optional description
3. Click **Publish Site** — re-renders the Quarto site on the server
4. The new photo appears live on the portfolio page immediately

---

## Updating Site Code

When changes are pushed to GitHub, pull and re-render on the server:

```bash
cd /srv/auggie-smith-photography
sudo -u shiny git pull origin main
sudo -u shiny quarto render
```
